routes.name: Deep snow country
routes.theme: Three weeks in the Alps and the snowy side
routes.tagline: Tokyo 3, Nagano 3, Takayama 3, Okuhida 3, Kanazawa 4 and Tokyo 4: snow monkeys, thatched villages, a ryokan New Year in deep snow and Kanazawa's gardens under their snow ropes.
routes.feel: Three days of Tokyo lights, then the shinkansen climbs into the mountains. In Nagano you watch the dawn service at Zenko-ji, the fit five walk the forest path to the snow monkeys, and Christmas Day is a trip to Matsumoto's black castle with the Alps behind it. The Hida line follows a white gorge to Takayama: morning markets, sake breweries, a day among the thatched farmhouses of Shirakawa-go. On 29 Dec a short bus ride takes you up to Okuhida, where the snow is deepest and New Year's Eve is a long dinner at a ryokan, with a private bath and a ropeway up to 2,156 m the day before. On the quiet 1 Jan you come down to Kanazawa for its slow, free New Year days in Kenroku-en. You end with four easy days in Tokyo and one last snow day at Echigo-Yuzawa.
activities: Tokyo: Christmas illuminations, Tsukiji outer market and Hama-rikyu on the Monday museums close, Asakusa and Ueno
Nagano: Zenko-ji at dawn and its pitch-dark o-kaidan passage, the Jigokudani snow monkeys, a day trip to Matsumoto Castle and Nakamachi, Obuse for Hokusai and chestnut sweets
Takayama: Takayama Jinya before it closes on 29 Dec, morning markets, Sanmachi sake breweries, Hida beef, a day trip to Shirakawa-go by bus
Okuhida: a ryokan New Year's Eve with private baths in deep snow, the Shin-Hotaka double-decker ropeway, Hirayu Great Falls, a guided snowshoe walk for the fit
Kanazawa: Kenroku-en free on 1–3 Jan with its yukitsuri snow ropes, the 21st Century Museum from 2 Jan, Higashi Chaya and gold leaf, Omicho's crab when it reopens on 5 Jan
Tokyo: Tokyo National Museum and the January Kabuki, shopping, and a snow-play day trip to GALA Yuzawa (75 minutes away)
routes.why: This is the route for a family that came to Japan for winter itself: it stays on the snowy side of the mountains for two weeks instead of dipping in and out. It suits the first-timers who want the postcard Japan of snow and thatch, and it gives Pedro and Fernanda a trip with no Kyoto or Hakone repeats at all.
routes.suits: João and Carolina (snow, monkeys, snowshoes), Carlos and Nadir (castle, villages, long walks in the snow), Tatiana (the classic winter images); Pedro and Fernanda get an all-new trip, though Fernanda has the most ice to manage of any option.
routes.trade: No Kyoto, Nara or Fuji at all, so the first-timers miss Japan's temple capital and the famous mountain. There is more ice underfoot for Fernanda than on the main route, and New Year's Eve is about an hour from the nearest hospital with obstetrics rather than in a city. Five moves, and the 1 Jan journey is close to four hours.

stay_notes.tokyo: Arrival plus two full days to get over the flight; the city comes back at the end, so this first visit can stay light.
stay_notes.nagano: Arrival afternoon at Zenko-ji, then one day for the snow monkeys and one for Matsumoto Castle, which is open until 28 Dec and closed 29–31 Dec. Nagano is a flat city with trains in every direction and a Red Cross hospital.
stay_notes.takayama: Three nights so the Jinya (closed from 29 Dec), the old town and a full Shirakawa-go day all fit before New Year, without rushing on icy streets.
stay_notes.okuhida: Fixed by the calendar: in by 29 Dec on a one-hour bus, out on the quiet 1 Jan. Three nights gives one ropeway day, one slow day and New Year's Eve itself.
stay_notes.kanazawa: 1–4 Jan are slow days everywhere; Kanazawa is a home-coming city, not a resort, so it stays calm. Kenroku-en is free, the 21st Century Museum reopens on 2 Jan and Omicho fully reopens on 5 Jan, the morning you leave.
stay_notes.tokyo:2: Four nights so the museums closed in December can be seen, a snow-play day at Echigo-Yuzawa fits, and the last night is close to the airport.

tokyo.longer: A Nikko or Kawagoe day before the snow
tokyo.shorter: Straight into the mountains on the second morning, still jet-lagged
tokyo.note: Full but gentle; Monday 21 Dec is the market-and-gardens day because museums close.

nagano.longer: A Nozawa Onsen snow day with sledding and the village baths, or Togakushi's cedar avenue
nagano.shorter: Matsumoto or the monkeys drops out
nagano.note: Every day has a clear plan; the monkey morning is long for the walkers, so Fernanda's afternoon is free.

takayama.shorter: Shirakawa-go squeezed into the travel day, or the Jinya missed

kanazawa.shorter: Leaving on 4 Jan, a peak day on the Hokuriku line

tokyo:2.shorter: The Yuzawa snow day or the late museum evening goes
tokyo:2.note: 8 Jan is deliberately free for shopping and packing; send big bags to the airport by 6 Jan.

checks.peak_day_moves: One: Takayama to Okuhida on 29 Dec, a one-hour local bus that heads away from the crowds; the 1 Jan journey is on the quietest travel day of the year.
checks.risks: Mountain roads: the Okuhida buses run in heavy snow but can be delayed, and the Shin-Hotaka ropeway stops in strong wind. Okuhida ryokan rooms for seven over New Year are tight in mid-October, and the nearest obstetrics (Takayama Red Cross) is 45–60 minutes away on a snowy road during the holiday closures. Ice everywhere for Fernanda.

routes.name: The western onsen trail
routes.theme: Three great hot-spring towns, with Kyoto between
routes.tagline: Tokyo 2, Hakone 2, Kyoto 4, Kinosaki 4, Arima 4 and Tokyo 4: ten nights in onsen ryokan, a yukata New Year in Kinosaki and Japan's oldest hot spring for the first days of 2027.
routes.feel: After two Tokyo days the trip slows straight away: a Romancecar to Hakone, an in-room bath, Fuji over the ridges and the Open-Air Museum. Christmas Eve is in Kyoto, with four days of temples, Gion lanes and Nara's deer before everything closes. On 28 Dec a direct train runs north to Kinosaki, the willow-lined canal town where everyone walks between baths in yukata and wooden sandals. It is liveliest at New Year: crab dinners, the ropeway, a half day in the castle town of Izushi, then New Year's Eve at the inn. On the quiet 1 Jan you move to Arima, in the hills behind Kobe, for the first-bath ceremony on 2 Jan, a Kobe day and Himeji Castle. Four Tokyo nights close the trip.
activities: Tokyo: Tsukiji outer market and Hama-rikyu on the Monday, Ginza food halls and the Christmas lights
Hakone: an in-room bath for each couple, the Hakone Open-Air Museum and its foot bath, Pola Museum, Fuji from Lake Ashi
Kyoto: Higashiyama and Kiyomizu-dera, Fushimi Inari's lower shrines early, Arashiyama, and a Nara day before the New Year crowds
Kinosaki: the canal-side public baths in yukata (others) and private baths at the inn (her), snow-crab kaiseki, the ropeway and Onsen-ji, a half day in Izushi for sara soba
Arima: the Irizome-shiki first-bath ceremony on 2 Jan, Gin-no-yu's cooler carbonated bath, the hill lanes, a Kobe day and Himeji Castle on 4 Jan
Tokyo: Tokyo National Museum, New Year Kabuki, last shopping
routes.why: This route is built around bathing well, which suits Fernanda better than any snow walk: three onsen towns where she can soak in private, gently and often, while the others try the famous public baths. Kyoto gives the first-timers their temples in between, and Kinosaki at New Year is one of Japan's happiest places to be.
routes.suits: Fernanda (private baths, flat Kinosaki, cooked crab), Carlos and Nadir (bath-hopping in yukata, Kyoto, Himeji), Tatiana and Carolina (the ryokan life); João gets Himeji and Kobe but little snow.
routes.trade: No Kanazawa, Takayama, Shirakawa-go or real snow: Kinosaki may be white, the rest probably not. Hakone and Kyoto are repeats for Pedro and Fernanda. Ten ryokan nights make it the dearest of these three, and the last move from Arima to Tokyo is about four hours.

stays.note: Rooms with their own bath; Gora or Sengokuhara

routes.nye: At a Kinosaki ryokan on a two-night New Year plan: snow-crab dinner (cooked for her), toshikoshi soba, osechi on 1 Jan. The town is at its liveliest, with families in yukata walking the canal between the public baths late into the night; Fernanda uses the inn's private bath, which in Kinosaki is plain heated water she can set to her own temperature.

stay_notes.tokyo: Arrival plus one full day; Tokyo returns for four nights at the end, so the start is just a soft landing.
stay_notes.hakone: Two nights in a ryokan is the classic length: one full day for the museums and two dawns for a clear Fuji, before the holiday rush.
stay_notes.kyoto: Four nights while the temples are calm and before the 29 Dec closures: Higashiyama, Fushimi Inari, Arashiyama and a Nara day.
stay_notes.kinosaki: Fixed by the calendar: in on 28 Dec, before the peak days, and out on the quiet 1 Jan. The town is small, so the four days are baths, crab, the ropeway, Izushi and doing very little.
stay_notes.arima: In on 1 Jan, out on 5 Jan after the return rush. Arima itself is a day; the other days are the 2 Jan ceremony, Kobe and Himeji, each under an hour away.
stay_notes.tokyo:2: The museums closed in December, Kabuki from 2 Jan, and a calm last night close to the airport.

tokyo.longer: A gentler start before the first move
tokyo.shorter: Not possible: the first stay needs two nights
tokyo.note: One full day, used for the market and gardens since museums close on Mondays.

hakone.longer: A second Fuji morning and the Okada Museum
hakone.shorter: One night only, packing again the next morning
hakone.note: Full but easy; she should not get off the ropeway at Owakudani because of the volcanic gas.

kyoto.longer: Uji and its tea houses, or a slower Arashiyama
kyoto.note: Four full days; 28 Dec morning is Nishiki market before the train.

kinosaki.shorter: Moving on 29–31 Dec, the busy days
kinosaki.note: Honestly a slow four days: 29 Dec and 31 Dec have little planned beyond baths and walks, which is the point.

arima.shorter: Leaving on 4 Jan, the last peak day of the return rush

routes.name: Kyoto house and the sea
routes.theme: Three homes, two train rides, no rushing
routes.tagline: Tokyo 4, a Kyoto house for 12 and a seaside hotel in Kamakura for 4: the fewest moves of any option, with New Year lived like a Kyoto family.
routes.feel: Four unhurried days in Tokyo, then on Christmas Eve one train ride to Kyoto and a house with four bedrooms, a kitchen and two bathrooms near the Heian shrine. You stay twelve nights. Each day holds one easy thing: Higashiyama's lanes, Nara's deer, the trial ringing of Chion-in's great bell on 27 Dec, Uji's tea houses, a snow day above Lake Biwa for anyone who wants one. New Year's Eve is at home with soba, then a short walk to Yasaka Shrine for the sacred okera fire, while the fit ones queue to ring a temple bell at midnight. The New Year days are slow and local, with Kyoto University Hospital ten minutes away. On 5 Jan you move once more, to a hotel above the sea at Kamakura: the Great Buddha, the little Enoden train, and Fuji across the bay at sunset.
activities: Tokyo: Tsukiji outer market and Hama-rikyu, Meiji Jingu and Harajuku, Asakusa and Ueno, the Christmas lights
Kyoto: Higashiyama and Gion, Fushimi Inari's lower shrines, Arashiyama, the Kyoto National Museum from 2 Jan, Ohara's quiet Sanzen-in on New Year's Day
From the Kyoto house: Nara and Todai-ji, Uji's Byodo-in and tea, Omi-Hachiman's canals on Lake Biwa, Himeji Castle, and a Biwako Valley snow day for the fit
New Year in Kyoto: Chion-in's trial bell ringing on 27 Dec, the okera fire at Yasaka on 31 Dec, a bell to ring at Kodai-ji or Eikando for the fit ones
Kamakura: the Great Buddha, Hase-dera's lower garden, the Enoden along the coast, Enoshima, Fuji over Sagami Bay at sunset, and a Yokohama day
routes.why: This is the route built around Fernanda and the parents: only two moving days, a real home for the twelve middle nights, and every New Year night in a city with a university hospital. It still gives the first-timers Tokyo, Kyoto, Nara and Fuji, and it is the cheapest of these three by a distance.
routes.suits: Fernanda first of all (two moves, her own ground-floor room, the hospital close), Carlos and Nadir (Kyoto in depth, Kamakura's temples), Tatiana (a living room to share); João and Carolina can take the snow day and the long Fushimi climb.
routes.trade: No Kanazawa, Takayama, Shirakawa-go or onsen town, and no real snow. Tokyo and Kyoto are repeats for Pedro and Fernanda, and New Year's Eve is a home dinner rather than a ryokan. Twelve nights in one city means some days with very little planned.

stays.note: Four-bedroom machiya near Okazaki and the Heian shrine; New Year's Eve at home
Sea-view hotel at Shichirigahama; about an hour to Haneda

routes.nye: At the Kyoto house, argued on purpose: it is Japan's great New Year city, the house has a kitchen and a table for seven, and Kyoto University Hospital is ten minutes away when clinics are closed. Order an osechi box from a department store by mid-December, have toshikoshi soba at home or early at a soba shop, then walk to Yasaka Shrine around 19:30 for the okera fire before the midnight crowds. The fit ones queue for a bell they can ring (Kodai-ji, Chishaku-in or Eikando) while Fernanda goes home to bed.

stay_notes.tokyo: Arrival plus three easy days; Tokyo is not repeated at the end, so the first-timers get their Tokyo here while the Christmas lights are on.
stay_notes.kyoto: Twelve nights so that nobody packs between Christmas and Epiphany: the house covers the calm days before 29 Dec, the closed days, and the reopening on 2–4 Jan, with a different day trip whenever the city feels small.
stay_notes.kamakura: In after the return rush, out to the airport in about an hour. Four nights gives the Great Buddha, Enoshima, a Yokohama or Tokyo day, and a free last day.

tokyo.shorter: The first-timers' only Tokyo shrinks to two days

new_regions.lodging_for_seven: Two or three rooms at one ryokan with private baths and a lift: Taketoritei Maruyama (eight private baths, rooms with open-air baths), Hyoe Koyokaku (large, rooms with open-air baths) or Arima Grand Hotel (a six-person room with two beds and four futons). About ¥180,000–300,000 per night for six with two meals; more on 1–2 Jan.
new_regions.hospital: Saiseikai Hyogo Prefectural Hospital (regional perinatal centre), 5-1-1 Fujiwaradai-nakamachi, Kita-ku, 078-987-2222, about 20 minutes by car; Kobe City Medical Center General Hospital (24-hour maternity emergency) on Port Island, about 35 minutes

notes: Ice and Fernanda on the snow route: the Jigokudani trail is packed snow and ice, often several centimetres thick, for about 45 minutes each way with a rough last stretch; the honest advice is that she waits in Shibu Onsen unless the trail is freshly packed, she has crampons and poles, someone's arm, and her doctor is relaxed about it. The same goes for Takayama's slushy streets (taxis and strap-on cleats), the Shirakawa-go viewpoint (take the shuttle), the Shin-Hotaka summit (stay inside the warm top station) and Okuhida's outdoor baths (use the indoor private bath; no walking on icy stone in sub-zero air). New Year's Eve in Okuhida is the one place in these three routes that is 45–60 minutes from obstetrics during the closures; if that worries anyone, the swap is a Takayama ryokan for 29 Dec–1 Jan (Takayama Red Cross is a 10-minute walk) with Okuhida as a day trip on 30 Dec. Rooms: everywhere assumes four rooms or a four-bedroom house for three couples and Tatiana; the Kanazawa (Itose, 4 bedrooms) and Kyoto (Waren Bettei or Wakaba, 4 bedrooms, 2 bathrooms) houses were chosen for that. Rough lodging totals for seven: snow about ¥2.3M, onsen about ¥3.7M (ryokan dinners included), slow about ¥2.5M, all inside the S$15,000-per-couple target. Rejected: Nozawa or Shibu for New Year (named inns full, chalets want 7-night minimums), an Echigo-Yuzawa stay at the end (its last night would be nearly two hours from the airport, so it is a day trip instead), Dogo Onsen on the onsen trail (it needs a flight or a 6-hour rail day back), Atami for the slow route's seaside (good ryokan with private baths, but no Great Buddha or Fuji over the sea; it swaps in cleanly if an onsen matters more). Uncertain: 2026–27 winter bus timetables in Hida, the Arima ceremony time, Biwako Valley's opening date, Matsumoto Castle's exact 2026 closing dates (sources say 29–31 Dec or 29 Dec–3 Jan), and whether Shonan Kamakura General Hospital takes obstetric emergencies at night (Yokohama's university hospitals are the back-up, 30 minutes away).
